parsed.rationale: Although `PlaybackController` and `TimeShiftablePlayer` share four members (`installRenderTap:()`, `isPlaying:Bool`, `makeAudioBufferStream:() -> AsyncStream<AVAudioPCMBuffer>`, `removeRenderTap:()`), the structural evidence explicitly records `shared_field_count: 0` and null Jaccard similarity, indicating the pipeline itself found no meaningful overlap threshold. More importantly, the two protocols model distinct domain concepts: `PlaybackController` is a high-level command interface with `play:(reason: PlaybackReason) throws`, `stop:(reason: PlaybackReason)`, `toggle:`, and `state:PlaybackState`, while `TimeShiftablePlayer` is a lower-level, time-aware player interface with `seek:`, `seekToLive:`, `secondsBehindLive:`, `maxLookbackSeconds:`, `stateStream:`, and `timePositionStream:` — members that have no counterpart in `PlaybackController`. Introducing a shared parent protocol would couple two intentionally separate abstractions (a controller-layer command surface vs. a time-shift-capable player surface) and would force any conformer of the parent to satisfy members from both domains. The coincidence of four low-level audio-tap and streaming helpers is structural only; the domain semantics diverge significantly.
